text:
sophia_support: Hey team, customer (Jordan) reports embeddings API returning dimension 1 for every item and billing spike. They sent this curl:
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \\\
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\
  -d '{\\"model\\":\\"embed-small\\",\\"input\\":\\"[\\\"a short doc\\\"]\\"}'

sophia_support: Response was 200 but vectors look like [[0.12],[0.34],[...]] (1-dim) and tokens usage jumped unusually high.

client_jordan: Yep, copy/paste from our frontend. We batch where some items are strings and some are arrays. Frontend might stringify arrays. Seeing this in prod after last deploy :/ 

maya_engineer: That curl shows the problem: the input field is a JSON-string of an array (i.e. double-encoded). API treats it as a single scalar string, then the client-side batching serialized each char? Usually double-encoded strings become 1 item -> 1-d vector or weird tokenization. Can you paste exact request body from server logs (raw)?

sophia_support: Pasted raw from logs:
{
  "model": "embed-small",
  "input": "[\"a short doc\"]",
  "user_id": "acct_123"
}

maya_engineer: Yep, confirmed double-encoded. Also mixed shapes in batch will make server map types differently. Example bad batch we saw previously: ["hello", "world", "[\"array\"]", ["ok"]]

sam_dev: Quick repro I ran locally:
Request A (bad):
{
  "model": "embed-small",
  "input": "[\"one\",\"two\"]"
}
=> Server returned embeddings length 1 per item (because it saw a single string), and token usage counted the inside chars.

Request B (good):
{
  "model": "embed-small",
  "input": ["one","two"]
}
=> Works, returns two vectors of dim 128.

maya_engineer: Recommend triage steps for support:
- Ask client to confirm their HTTP client isn't applying JSON.stringify twice (common in JS when passing array to fetch body already stringified)
- Log raw request body (we already did)
- Reproduce with a local curl using the exact body
- If they insist the payload is fine, capture request headers (Content-Type) and any proxies altering body

client_jordan: We found the bug — our front-end serialization helper calls JSON.stringify on inputs regardless of type. Fix rolling now.

embed-bot: automated-note: detected unusual token usage pattern for acct_123 on 2026-03-12; flagged for billing review. Ticket: #T-8791

sophia_support: After fix, client retried with correct payload and got expected dims. customer confirms resolved. 

maya_engineer: For future, we should add a short doc blurb in SDK FAQ: \"avoid double JSON.stringify; pass arrays/strings directly to request body\" and a validation check server-side to reject JSON-stringified arrays with a 400 and helpful message. Filing follow-up PR.

sam_dev: Patch idea: on server, if Content-Type==application/json and typeof input==\"string\" and input.match(/^\[.*\]$/s) then respond 400 with: \"input appears to be a JSON-encoded array; pass array directly to \"input\". See docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/embeddings/input-format\" 

sophia_support: Marking thread resolved, billing bot already pinged finance for review of the spike. :thumbsup:

client_jordan: Thanks all, saved our weekly job from overbilling. Really appreciate quick turnaround!
